desc:
Return the number of different non-empty palindromic substrings of s. A substring that occurs at several places is counted once.

For example, s = "aaa" has three distinct palindromic substrings (a, aa, aaa), and s = "abaab" has five: a, b, aba, aa, baab.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Storing every palindromic substring in a set takes O(n²) time and memory in the worst case. Try to bound how many new palindromes a single new character can create.

Appending one character to a string creates at most one new distinct palindromic substring: the longest palindromic suffix is the only candidate, all shorter palindromic suffixes already occurred earlier.

Build a palindromic tree (eertree): nodes are distinct palindromes, edges add the same character on both sides, and a suffix link points to the longest proper palindromic suffix. The number of nodes (minus the two roots) is the answer.
editorial: Claim: when you append the character s[i], at most one new palindrome appears. Any new palindromic suffix other than the longest one is a prefix-mirror of a longer palindromic suffix, hence it already occurred earlier in the string. So the total number of distinct palindromes is at most n, and we only have to detect whether the longest palindromic suffix of s[0..i] is new.

The eertree has two roots (length -1 and length 0), and for each node a map of children by letter and a suffix link. To process s[i]: start from the node of the longest palindromic suffix of the previous prefix and follow suffix links until a node v with s[i - len(v) - 1] == s[i]. If the child by s[i] exists, move to it. Otherwise create it with length len(v) + 2 and compute its suffix link by following links from link[v] in the same way.

Both walks are amortised O(1) per character because the depth of the 'current suffix' node increases by at most one per step. Total time O(n) (times the alphabet size for the children dictionaries) and O(n) space. The answer is the number of nodes created.
solution:
def countDistinctPalindromes(s):
    length = [-1, 0]
    link = [0, 0]
    nxt = [{}, {}]
    last = 1
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        cur = last
        while True:
            l = length[cur]
            if i - l - 1 >= 0 and s[i - l - 1] == ch:
                break
            cur = link[cur]
        if ch in nxt[cur]:
            last = nxt[cur][ch]
            continue
        new = len(length)
        length.append(length[cur] + 2)
        nxt.append({})
        if length[new] == 1:
            link.append(1)
        else:
            q = link[cur]
            while True:
                l = length[q]
                if i - l - 1 >= 0 and s[i - l - 1] == ch:
                    break
                q = link[q]
            link.append(nxt[q][ch])
        nxt[cur][ch] = new
        last = new
    return len(length) - 2
